# Multi-Level Work Breakdown Structure (WBS)

> **Companion design document**. This document accompanies
> [RFC-039 Compiler Architecture Refactor](../../rfc/accepted/039-compiler-architecture.md),
> expanding the RFC’s phase sequence into **independently committable and independently verifiable**
> three-level tasks.
>
> RFC-039’s main text is the sole authority for phase order and acceptance gates; this document is
> responsible only for breaking the work down to an executable granularity and registering conflicts
> that remain undecided.

## Positioning and Scope

| Level       | Count       | Meaning                                                                                            |
| ----------- | ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Level 1** | 11 (P0–P10) | Phases, corresponding one-to-one with the phase sequence in RFC-039                                |
| **Level 2** | 73          | Task groups: work groups broken down by phase, capable of being staffed and archived independently |
| **Level 3** | 262         | Work units that can be committed and verified independently                                        |

**Reserved gaps (not reclaimed)**: P4 has no `4.7`/`4.8`, and P8 has no `8.1`; after the LALRPOP
route was withdrawn, `8.4` / `8.5` / `8.6` were also left unused (2026-11-25). None of the three has
had a corresponding entry since the WBS was established—the entire history of this document has zero
matches for the three headings `**4.7` / `**4.8` / `**8.1` (verifiable with
`git log -S'**4.7' -- docs/src/dev/architecture/09-execution-wbs.md`), and there are no
repository-wide references either. `8.1` corresponds precisely to phase 1 of `05` (test revival and
completion): that phase was split into P1 (`1.1`–`1.3`) and `8.8`, so P8’s numbering is aligned with
its phase numbers (phase 0 → `8.0`, phase 2 → `8.2`, and so on).

**Covered by this document**: task decomposition, dependencies, parallelization groups, and
acceptance-criterion bindings.

**Not covered by this document**: the design rationale for tasks (see `02`–`08`) or the
justification for phase order (see RFC-039).

**Registration convention (effective 2026-10-12)**: every newly registered level-2/level-3 entry
**must contain two fields**—“**Owning phase**” (the P phase to which it truly belongs, which may
differ from the containing section) and “**Blocks the mainline**”; `registered, awaiting scheduling`
is no longer the default state, and an unmarked entry is considered **not schedulable**. Numbers
must be **unique throughout the document** (cross-track tasks use their track number, such as
`029g.x`, and must not occupy an `N.x` number).

**Closure registration (effective 2026-11-24)**: a checked entry contains only four items—the task
id, status, **implementation commit short hash** (7 characters), and issue number (only when
applicable)—on one line:
`- [x] **3.24.1 Remaining Pattern-Matching Completion** ✅ 4d608df3 (issue #405)`. **Do not write
the fix, the criterion chain, gate values, file line numbers, test names, or review conclusions**:
those belong in the commit message (`git show <short-hash>`). This table is a board, not a process
diary. **Do not write ruling tags or restate conclusions**: “user ruling A/B/C,” “option A,” “final
implementation is…” and similar text must not appear in this table—the board answers only “complete
or not”; consult the commit message and RFC-039’s decision registry for rulings and outcomes.

**Short hashes are authoritative only after push**: closure entries record the short hash on
`origin/dev` after the push completes. The order is **push the implementation commit first, then
write the closure entry** (see [commit-convention](../commit-convention.md), “Take the commit number
after push”). The closure commit itself does not carry a number—a self-reference is impossible.

**The count column contains numbers only**: the level-1/level-2/level-3 counts in
`Positioning and Scope` contain only the current values; increment/decrement history (`+1 = …`) does
not belong in the table.

## Current State: Gaps Found During Decomposition

While consolidating the “implementation essentials” of eight documents into this table, **five hard
gaps in the documentation system itself** were found. All have now been resolved:

| #   | Gap                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Resolution                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| --- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| G1  | **P5 has no implementation steps whatsoever**. RFC-039 defines P5 (checker splitting) and its acceptance criterion (C1 zero-diff), but none of the seven documents describes how the split should be performed; the directory tree in `01-routing.md` contains one `annotations.rs` entry, the only mention in the entire batch                                                                                        | P5’s steps are supplied by this document (see below)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| G2  | **The three `include!` conversion sites have conflicting ownership and no implementation**. RFC-039 lists it under P4; `02` assigns the reference to itself; `06` S7 also lists it. However, the change list in `02` (6 additions + 20 modifications) contains **no `semantic_tokens.rs`**                                                                                                                             | The implementation steps belong to §P5 5.1 of this document (after P4 is complete); references in RFC-039 and `06` now point here                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| G3  | **Three coexisting lists of CI scripts**. `RFC` lists 4 `scripts/ci/*.py`; `01` lists 4 scripts + 1 `cargo test`; `07` lists another 4 checks (all with different names); `04` also previously listed `check-synth-boundary.py` (that script was cancelled by the user on 2026-11-24). After deduplication there are **at least 9 new scripts and no unified list**; `check-obligations.py` is owned by both P4 and P9 | See §P9 of this document for the unified list (10 active scripts, each owned by one phase); all other documents now refer to this table                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| G4  | **Conflict over the fate of `precedence_inline.rs`**. `06` counts it among the “1,005 lines that must be revived,” while B6 in the same document says it “must be deleted together with” the `Precedence` enum; `05` advocates deletion                                                                                                                                                                                | **Revive in P1, retain in P8** (decision registry C1; Pratt is no longer removed)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| G5  | **Conflicting descriptions of the L2 goal**. RFC-039 and this directory’s index describe “grammar-driven syntax,” but `05` self-assesses: “**did not adopt true grammar-driven parsing (LALRPOP); it only achieved declarative table lookup**”                                                                                                                                                                         | Consolidated into **a declarative precedence table + an unambiguous language surface**: the full LALRPOP grammar-driven route was withdrawn (the two attempts produced 29 / 148 conflicts), and, following `05:648`, the work fell back to “retain Pratt + one declarative precedence table + cross-validation of two `BinOp` implementations from the same source”; see P8 8.3 |

## Target Design: Phase Sequence

```
P0 仓库维护机制与代码放置规程 08 ← 新增，先立规矩
P1 复活孤儿测试并修缺陷 06 §S1
P2 建立等价性判据基线 07 全部
P3 修正确性漏洞（最小方案） 02 §S3-漏洞半部
P4 阶段契约与统一 Driver 02
P5 checker 文件内拆分 02 + 本文补齐
P6 类型表示单一化 03
P7 中间表示 SSA 化 04 } 可并行
P8 前端范式变更 05 }
P9 防反弹门禁（含统一脚本清单） 01 §防反弹 + 08 §可机检规则
P10 其余清理与状态修正 06 §S2/S3/S4/S5/S6
```

**Reason for adding P0**: the three prohibitions (no fabrication / no endless filling / no patching
when a refactor is required) constrain every action in P1–P10. The rules must be established before
work begins; otherwise, when P1 revives tests, it will already be adding `mod` declarations to
`tests/mod.rs`—precisely the cause of the G4 conflict.

### P3 Fix Correctness Vulnerabilities (Minimal Approach)

Source: the vulnerability-fix half of [02](02-stage-contract.md) §Implementation Essentials S3 ＋
**the silent-discard audit of 2026-10-07 (3.4)**

> **Semantic-correction routing (D59, decision of 2026-10-11)**: if this track or any later phase
> discovers a defect for which “the old behavior did not count as success”—**A silent failure / B
> silent mismatch / C undefined behavior and resource loss** (crash, stack overflow, silently
> returning the wrong answer)—it **may be fixed alongside the refactor**, provided all four
> requirements are met: ① red before green (the red criterion must exist first and genuinely fail);
> ② no change to the externally observable behavior of programs that “previously compiled
> successfully and ran correctly” (they must not become failures, and their existing diagnostic
> codes/text/exit codes must not be changed or removed); ③ registration in the same commit (this
> entry states the error type + a revision note for that phase + the PR required-block “Error Type”
> line); ④ regeneration of the baseline in the same commit + manual diff review. **The three
> categories D user-visible semantics / E external contract tables / F RFC-level design changes must
> still receive a ruling first. For the expanded criteria and A–F whitelist, see
> [07 §Routing Criteria for Semantic Corrections](07-equivalence-oracle.md); the approach of
> “default super-refactor + post-hoc registration” is not adopted** (the rationale is in RFC-039
> D59: a zero red criterion cannot distinguish a fix from a regression and conflicts with both “C5′
> does not exist” and “no relaxation whatsoever”).

**Acceptance**: the vulnerability criterion turns green, and **removing the fix must turn it red
again**. **Risk**: the new E4018 on the multi-file path is a breaking change.

**3.4 acceptance**: 3.4.1 / 3.4.2 must have red criteria first (changing code first is forbidden);
3.4.3 is manual review; 3.4.4–3.4.8 follow C2/C3 and the 9.2 gate in P9. **Risk**: the new
diagnostic in 3.4.1 is a behavioral change and requires the corpus differential baseline and
CHANGELOG to be updated in sync.

> **Stop-the-bleeding path**: P3 need not wait for all of P2. The only hard prerequisites for
> 3.1/3.2 are **2.3.2 (multi-file corpus layer) + 2.4.1/2.4.3 (two red criteria)**;
> 2.1/2.2/2.3.1/2.3.3 (IR verifier, snapshots, single-file differential testing, performance
> baseline) can proceed in parallel with P3. Stopping the bleeding for correctness vulnerabilities
> (such as `Sorted(3)` passing silently) must not be blocked by snapshot-infrastructure
> construction. 3.3 (panic-to-diagnostic conversion) has no prerequisites and may land at any time.

### External Track RFC-029g: Remove `pub` and Automatic Binding (External Track / #399 — Ordering Constraint D56)

Source: [RFC-029g](../../rfc/accepted/029g-remove-pub-and-auto-bind.md) (accepted 2026-10-02,
implementation not started), [#399](https://github.com/ChenXu233/YaoXiang/issues/399). **This track
is not a design item of the refactor itself; it is a specification-compliance deletion forced by an
ordering constraint**, and is separate from P10 S5 “reduce the visibility of `pub` items” (narrowing
Rust’s `pub(crate)`).

**Why it must be completed before P4 as a whole**: 029g’s deletion surface overlaps with the
rewriting surfaces of all four refactor phases; reversing the order means redoing the same deletions
and baseline updates on the new syntax / new checker layout / new SSA IR.

| ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

| AST `is_pub` ×2 (`Assign` / `TypeDefinition`)                      | `parser/ast.rs`                                                                                                    | **P6 6.5 dead AST variants** + P8 + D1 directory rename (`parser/ast.rs` → top-level `src/ast/`)                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `auto_bind_to_type` and the pub branch of `collect_exports`        | `typecheck/checker.rs`, `environment.rs`                                                                           | **P5** (`include!`→true `mod` and checker splitting are **pure relocation**; the pub branch will be moved unchanged into the new files)                                                                                                                               |
| Dead-code exemption `exempt_pub` / `is_exported` and role dispatch | `typecheck/passes/dead_code.rs`, `module/orchestrator.rs` (inside `check_project`)                                 | **P4 4.2.2** (`check_project` slimming)                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `Public` modifier in `semantic_tokens`                             | `typecheck/checker/semantic_tokens.rs`                                                                             | **P4 4.2.6** + P5 + 4.6 (D55)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `is_pub` ignored by `ir_gen` when binding                          | `middle/core/ir_gen.rs`                                                                                            | **P7** (SSA conversion of `ir_gen.rs`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| 31 occurrences of `pub` in `src/std/`                              | `std/list.yx` / `json.yx` / `option.yx` / `result.yx`                                                              | No phase directly changes them, but **P6’s hard acceptance criterion requires zero differences in `src/std/` (`git diff --stat src/std/` is empty; direct-drive tests under `tests/` are excepted; see the P6 hard acceptance section)**—they can only land before P6 |

**Acceptance (behavior changes; red criterion first)**:

1. **Red before green**: each of the two behavior changes must first land a red criterion before
   code changes—① `pub` changes from “silently accepted” to a parse error; ② an unreferenced
   top-level binding in a Lib/Script role newly reports W1001 (previously pub items were absolutely
   exempt).
2. **The test count must not decrease**: when deleting the `exempt_pub` case from
   `typecheck/passes/tests/dead_code.rs` and the `is_pub` fixture, they must be replaced by
   equivalent new cases.
3. **Baseline in the same commit**: diagnostic-set changes (new parse error + new W1001) ⇒ update
   the corpus differential baseline (`tests/baselines/corpus-parity.jsonl`) and CHANGELOG in the
   same commit; IR snapshots are expected to have zero differences, and any non-zero difference must
   be explained.
4. **Independent revert unit**: the entire batch occupies one commit group and must not be mixed
   with other phases (DoD 6).
5. `cargo test` / `clippy -D warnings` / `python scripts/rfc/check_tracking.py` are all green.

**Ordering**: it overlaps with 3.4 in files (`checker.rs`, `environment.rs`) ⇒ the two must be
serial and cannot run in parallel; **the whole track must precede P4** (RFC-039 D56). The 029g track
does not depend on 3.4; implementers may choose which to start based on the context at hand.

> **Commit correspondence (2026-10-08)**: the incorporation of this section (the P3.5 chapter +
> main-chain/constraint row) was merged into `97071c81b` together with RFC-039 D56 while cleaning
> the parallel-stream worktree—the message of that commit records “3.4 additional registration +
> D57/D58 decisions filed,” without mentioning this track. History is not rewritten; as with the
> existing style (the `d5b18390` precedent, see the P2 implementation note), it is registered in
> place as evidence for later bisection.

|                                                  | 4.4.4 The SMT shared-solver observation ledger `ConsumerStats`/`CONSUMER_STATS`: every production-path point writes, and the production side has zero readers (the only read site is `proof/smt/tests/shared.rs`). **Decision ① of 2026-10-24: retain it**—write “the sole consumer = tests” as a documentation contract (preserving the observable-criterion carrier required by D58); decision ②, “delete it,” is not adopted (that would require changing 4.4.2’s acceptance criterion at the same time; the rationale is recorded in the 4.4 closure “sixteen”). **Terminal state**: the three contract sentences are written into the module header of `src/frontend/core/typecheck/proof/smt/backend.rs` and the relevant item documentation comments—① the write surface = one atomic increment for every acquisition through the shared interface; ② the read surface is **only** `proof/smt/tests/shared.rs` (zero calls in production code); ③ `SolverConsumer::ALL` is a **test-only constant**, and production code must not depend on it; **zero behavioral change** (only comments are changed, and 4.4.2’s acceptance number is unchanged; issue |                                                  | 4.9.9 A cross-unit single-definition method called with **named arguments** loses its formal-parameter-name table (registered 2026-11-25, discovered during 7c closure): calling a cross-unit (registry-injected) method with named arguments reports `E1014 Function '…' has no parameter named '…' (available: )`—the name table is empty; positional calls to the same method work normally, as do named-argument calls within a single file. Minimal reproduction: `lib.yx` defines `Point.scale_by: (self: &Point, k: Float) -> Float`, and `main.yx` contains `p.scale_by(k = 2.0)` ⇒ E1014, while `p.scale_by(2.0)` ⇒ 6.0. **D59 classification: category C (primary fix) + category D checklist (all conflict forms rejected, pending a user ruling)** (the old behavior was unsuccessful: named arguments were silently dropped before runtime failure or a silent wrong value; positional calls do not consume the name table, but under **name-level ambiguity** (a same-named type provided by ≥2 modules), they belong to another criterion: when the host module and candidate-providing module have the same source, allow; when they have different sources and the two candidate signatures are identical, allow; conflict forms (name-level ambiguity, ≥2 providers) always reject positional calls with E1107 (see item ④ below)). The mechanism is a **consumer-side key mismatch**—the IR-generation-side formal-parameter-name lookup has only three sources: the current unit’s `fn_param_names` / the leaf name / the module export surface; the first segment of the method key `{Type}.{method}` is a type name, not a module key, and therefore never hits the export surface. **Root cause and fix (a single point; no second name table)**: ① `AstToIrGenerator::lookup_param_info` (`src/middle/lower/query.rs`) gains the source `method_param_info`—obtain the formal-parameter-name table from the existing sole cross-unit carrier `ModuleInfo::method_overloads` (three aligned vectors for candidate ↔ mangled name ↔ formal names; `extract_module_info` ← `method_overload_snapshot`, the same source as the typecheck injection surface), keyed by `{module}.{Type}.{method}[#N]`; the call site (`src/middle/lower/expr/call.rs`) uses `method_dispatch_name`’s definition-unit qualified name as the lookup key; ② the candidate-injection surface’s narrowing rule pairs by target (definition-side type name), while candidates imported by alias continue to be injected; ③ **provider priority** (a bare-name provider with `local == target` takes priority, and an alias fills the position only when the bare name is absent; same-level multiple modules with the same full name are skipped) is now the **single shared point** `frontend::module::import_face::TypeCandidateProviders`—the injection surface (`driver::arms.rs`) and the consumer side (`middle::lower::query`) read the same source and no longer evolve independently; ④ **same-source criterion** (`method_source_mismatch`, `src/middle/lower/query.rs`): let `winner` = the providing module selected by the candidate-injection surface and `owner` = the module to which the receiver belongs (the same ownership decision as `method_dispatch_name`)—`owner == winner` ⇒ allow (typecheck and IR use candidates from the same module; the bare-name positional call belongs here, measured 2.0 + 2.0 = 4.0); `owner != winner` ⇒ allow only when the two modules have **exactly identical candidate signatures** for the key (candidate selection does not affect type checking, and the value is determined by the receiver’s owning unit—the existing behavior for cross-unit same-named types introduced through inline aliases), otherwise reject loudly (the existing E1107). **Positional arguments with identical signatures are still allowed** (the 4.9.8 fixture 0/0; the value is determined by the receiver’s unit). Conflict forms (name-level ambiguity, ≥2 providers, full-name skip in the injection surface) take the **conflict branch**: named arguments produce E1014; positional arguments **always produce E1107**—regardless of actual-argument types, arity, or which side owns the receiver, the decision depends only on the import surface, so the result is deterministic for the same input. The IR no longer duplicates typecheck’s type-compatibility rules (the previous narrow compatibility criterion has been removed); deterministic companion: `all_method_bindings` merges by ascending module key and no longer randomly overwrites entries according to HashMap iteration order. **Delivery (this entry is complete)**: ① cross-unit method named arguments obtain the **declaration-time formal-parameter-name table** (positive capability, `p.scale_by(k = 2.0)` ⇒ 6.0); ② **name-level ambiguity / conflict forms are deterministically rejected with loud diagnostics** (named arguments E1014, positional arguments E1107, with the decision depending only on the import surface); ③ deterministic repair of `all_method_bindings` sorting by module key (the same input no longer yields different results due to HashMap iteration order). **Completed on 2026-11-26 (fix rounds 1–6 + review rounds 1–6 + closure registration)**; review round 6 independently passed (criteria and registration completeness). **Category-D checklist (each item recorded; based on the user’s direction approved on 2026-11-25—name-level ambiguity is always rejected loudly; recording each item here does not mean each is approved)**: seven cases in conflict / mixed forms that previously worked and now produce E1107—① Int→Float widening (literal and variable actual arguments, pre-t5 0/0 prints 2.5); ② whole-import owner (`use c` + `c.Temp(...)`, 0/0 prints 9); ③ mixed form with compatible owner (0/0 prints 200 / 2.5); ④ same parameters and same return type (0/0 prints 200); ⑤ zero-actual-argument same signature `tag()` (0/0 prints 111); ⑥ owner accepts Int + another provider accepts Float + actual argument Int (0/0 prints 200); ⑦ mixed/conflict forms with same parameters and different return types (0/0 prints 200). **Category C (listed separately; the old behavior was unsuccessful and is fixed independently under this criterion)**: the two providers have different formal-parameter types (pre-t5 was already indeterminate: 0/0 prints 200.0 / E1002 / runtime failure); arity mismatch (pre-t5 0/0 prints 300 = a silent wrong value from an extra actual argument being dropped); named arguments (pre-t5 silently dropped arguments and then produced runtime E6007 → now E1014). **Named arguments** under name-level ambiguity (a same-named type provided by ≥2 modules) are still always rejected loudly (the shared criterion’s empty-table exit = the existing E1014): the name-table source is untrustworthy, so name-based checking is impossible; ⑤ **fallback for “never silently discard named arguments”**: `reject_named_args_without_param_names` reuses the shared criterion `arg_binding::bind_args_to_params`’s empty-table exit (the existing E1014, with `available` using the same empty-string semantics), and is connected to the IR-side’s four arms that “have named arguments but cannot obtain the formal-parameter-name table”—the RFC-004 binding arm, the namespace arm, the ordinary method arm without overload resolution, and the ordinary **static** function arm; built-in container construction arms (`src/middle/lower/expr/container.rs`) also reject named arguments other than `len`; ⑥ **the fallback exclusion surface is determined by binding identity**: closure-value bindings (`closure_fn_names` in `stmt.rs`: the binding value is written as an `=>` lambda and the declaration has no value parameters), current-unit top-level function bindings (`declared_fn_names`), and **named nested-function declarations** (`nested_functions` entries) do **not** enter the fallback—all three have the old behavior of “compiles successfully and ignores named arguments,” and reclassifying them as compile-time errors falls under D59 category D; all three are registered together as known gaps (D60 ② “should report but does not,” category A). **Visible changes (list each one; do not merge them into “no behavioral change”)**: ① cross-unit method named arguments (bare import / alias import / two overload candidates) change from an empty-table E1014 to name-based slot binding (measured 6.0 / 30); ② an alias-imported method (single provider) with named arguments changes from silently dropping arguments (runtime `E6007`) to name-based slot binding (6.0); ③ g9g generic curried-method named arguments change from silently dropping arguments (`b.v` reads Void, runtime `E6007 Void vs Int`) to compile-time E1014 (category C); ④ cross-unit ordinary-function named arguments silently drop arguments → E1014 (category C); ⑤ const-generic receiver-method named arguments silently drop arguments → E1014 (category C; the **positional** form of the same shape still fails due to an existing independent defect, outside this task); ⑥ built-in container construction `Vec(Int)(foo = 3)` silently ignores them → E1014 (category C; `Vec(Int)(len = 3)` still 0/0 and has a value assertion `v.length == 3`); ⑦ whole-module import (`use lib` + `lib.Circle(...)`) named arguments are silently dropped → E1014 (category C); ⑧ **named arguments on name-level-ambiguous types** always produce E1014; positional arguments: `owner == winner` and “`owner != winner` but candidate signatures are identical” are allowed (value assertions 4.0 / 200 / 20); different sources with inconsistent signatures, or conflict forms, always produce E1107 (three measured cases of silent wrong value are eliminated: differing formal-parameter types, differing arity, differing return types; the conflict-form cost list is in this entry’s category-D checklist); ⑨ closure-value bindings (top-level `f = () => 7` and those inside function bodies), block-body function declarations (`f: (a: Int) -> Int = { 7 }`), and named nested-function declarations (body ignores formal parameters) **retain the old behavior** for named arguments (ignored, measured result 7), with no reclassification. **Residual / known gaps**: named arguments on the above three declaration surfaces are still silently ignored (category A, D60 ② “should report but does not”); the formal-parameter-name table for named nested functions is not yet connected to `lookup_param_info`; `E1014` text limitation: an empty `available` means “the IR did not obtain a name table,” not “the function truly has no such parameter”; the text is unchanged and the diagnostic surface is not expanded this time; the same-source criterion’s signature comparison is structural equivalence (it does not compare implementations), and the residual risk of “identical signature, different implementation” is documented in 4.9.10. **Criteria**: 30 driver-level direct-drive tests in `src/driver/tests/named_args_cross_unit_method.rs` (cross-unit named arguments / alias import / selecting a name from two overload candidates / table-driven multiple columns / whole-module import / RFC-004 binding / mixed-import named arguments E1014 + bare-name-side positional arguments 0/0 (4.0) + alias-side formal-parameter type/arity/return-type three cases E1107 + alias-side same-named formal parameter E1014 / two bare-name providers in conflict E5006 / top-level closure old behavior Int(7) / closure inside a function body old behavior / named nested function ignoring formal parameters old behavior Int(7) / container-construction rejection + `len` value assertion / two aliases in conflict (named E1014, positional always E1107) + seven conflict-boundary cases (Int→Float widening literal/variable, whole-import owner, mixed compatible owner, arity mismatch, zero-actual-argument tag(), owner Int + Float provider + Int actual argument) / **invariant criteria**: named arguments in ambiguous forms must fail + positional arguments with identical signatures 0/0 and dispatch to the receiver’s owning module (200 / 20)), a unit guard in `src/middle/lower/tests/query.rs` (an empty name table ⇒ `None`; deleting the guard turns it red), and project-level fixtures `tests/yaoxiang-multifile/named-args-cross-unit-method{,-alias-overload}`. **Completion revisions**: first fix `02ed42d2`, fallback and `method_param_info` hardening `091b835b`, mixed-import provider priority and container rejection `5edfb53e`, review round (name-level ambiguity rejection / closure-value identity / top-level closure / value assertions) `7e96a844`, this round’s same-source criterion and shared provider table `c861088e`, fix round 5 (conflict visibility / deterministic merge) `a056d30c`, fix round 6 (positional arguments in conflict forms always E1107) `9498ca98`, fix round 7 (completion of the category-D checklist and C/D classification, criteria +2) `8ec25cb1`, and this entry’s closure registration (review round 6 pass: criteria and registration completeness) = the commit to which this entry belongs. **Regression surface**: zero IR-snapshot drift, corpus parity 405 entries (403 existing entries byte-for-byte unchanged + 2 new fixtures), and the six dispatch criteria from 4.9.8 remain green; five unit tests in `src/frontend/module/import_face.rs` cover conflict alias / bare+alias two-level conflict providers/winner/provider_count/injected_pairs. | 4.9.7         | Criteria are documented in `src/driver/tests/named_args_cross_unit_method.rs` and this entry’s “Criteria”; |                                                  | 4.9.10 Undefined cross-unit method identity (registered 2026-11-25, confirmed as a structural issue during implementation of 4.9.9): the method candidate key `{Type}.{method}` does not include a module qualifier, so for same-named types across modules, three consumers—candidate injection (`arms.rs::visible_method_overloads`), typecheck’s formal-parameter-name/candidate matching, and IR dispatch (`method_dispatch_name`)—each **guess the provider by name**, and any change in one place moves the “silent wrong value” to another. The stop-the-bleeding criterion in 4.9.9 is: named arguments under name-level ambiguity always produce E1014; positional arguments—same source (candidate-providing module == receiver’s owning module) are allowed, different sources with identical candidate signatures are allowed, and **conflict forms (name-level ambiguity, ≥2 providers) always produce E1107** (the IR does not duplicate typecheck’s compatibility rules); the root-cause solution = upgrade the method key to a **module-qualified identity**, produce it from one location, and have the three locations only read it; this requires changing the key form of `overload_resolutions` and the mangled names (D59 **category D**, requires a ruling) ### P5 Splitting the checker into Files — Supplemented by This Document (Original Gap G1)

Source: RFC-039 definition + the directory tree in `01-routing.md` + the hard constraint (the
`pub(crate)` path of `collect_used_in_type` must not change)

- [x] **5.1 `include!` → true `mod`** (2 level-3 tasks)
- [x] **5.2 Extract `refinement`** (2 level-3 tasks)
- [x] **5.3 Extract `annotations`** (2 level-3 tasks)

| Level 2                     | Level 3                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Prerequisites | Acceptance                                                                                                                                |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 5.1 `include!` → true `mod` | 5.1.1 Change the `include!` at the end of `checker.rs` to a true `mod` declaration (do not hard-code a line anchor; it was measured at the end of the file at the time)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | P4 complete   | C1 zero-diff; `semantic_tokens.rs` gains module identity                                                                                  |
|                             | 5.1.2 Add `use super::*` or import each item individually (the `include!` era implicitly inherited the scope)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | 5.1.1         | `cargo build` is green                                                                                                                    |
| 5.2 Extract `refinement`    | 5.2.1 Move out the refinement blocks (three non-contiguous sections of the original `checker.rs`; now the single file `checker/refinement.rs`, containing `ReturnRefinement` / `RefinedWalkCtx`), leaving the retained surface and the six cross-boundary shared items in place                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | 5.1.1         | C1 zero-diff                                                                                                                              |
|                             | 5.2.2 Consolidate the refinement entry point into “`&self` + return diagnostics,” **without leaving the impl**: `collect_refined_binding_checks` (now `checker/refinement.rs`, `pub(super)`) no longer uses `&mut self` to write to the error channel implicitly; the diagnostic set is returned and propagated upward, with the single write site in the sole caller `check_module_impl` (`checker.rs`, symbolic location). **Reason for remaining in the impl**: the only field in this family is `self.env` (so detaching from the impl is technically feasible), but turning both the entry point and the walk into free functions would also move all call sites: `resolve_type_annotation` has 8 production sites (6 annotation paths + `refined_walk_stmt` + `collect_refined_var_names_in_stmt`), `collect_param_refinements` has 2 production sites + 1 test site, and this would create a reverse dependency from the “retained surface (signature collection)” to refinement—the opposite of the coupling this step is intended to eliminate | 5.2.1         | —                                                                                                                                         |
| 5.3 Extract `annotations`   | 5.3.1 Move out the 10-item annotation-validation family (now the single file `checker/annotations.rs`; `check_annotation_type_names` is the `pub(super)` entry point, the other 9 items are private to the family, and `is_predicate_head` is a free function within the family)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | 5.2.2         | C1 zero-diff                                                                                                                              |
|                             | 5.3.2 **Keep `collect_used_in_type` (`pub(crate)`) as `pub(crate)` and under the `checker` module path**: it is a **shared-surface** function (consumed by both `collect_function_signature` and the `inference/statements.rs:16` side), and 5.3.1, by measurement, **did not migrate it** ⇒ the “zero caller changes” criterion **was already satisfied**, so **do not add** a new `pub(crate) use annotations::*;` re-export. **Constraint retained**: if it is migrated with the family in the future (into annotations or another later batch), `checker.rs` must add `pub(crate) use annotations::*;` so that the existing import remains unchanged                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | 5.3.1         | **Zero caller changes** is this step’s hard acceptance criterion: `git diff src/frontend/core/typecheck/inference/statements.rs` is empty |

**Hard constraint**: `collect_used_in_type` is used across modules by `inference/statements.rs:16`.
**If** the function is migrated with the annotation family in the future, **then** `checker.rs` must
add `pub(crate) use annotations::*;` so that the import remains unchanged; by measurement, 5.3 did
**not** migrate it, so this batch did not add a re-export (the criterion was already satisfied).

**Only split confirmed large blocks.** Do not split modules that are only 200–400 lines long—this
adds navigation cost, reduces cohesion, and yields no decoupling benefit. The remaining submodules
(signatures / type_defs / imports) await the files growing back to 1,500 lines before being split.

**6.9 Model and Invariants (First-Principles Rewrite, 2026-11-13)**

> **Model**: D62’s end state is a **unified item world**—type positions and value positions share
> the same set of compile-time items. One strength declaration produces one quantifier reading
> `q ∈ {0,1,ω}`; `q` is the **sole input** to slot allocation, and the call-site actual-argument
> view and implementation-head binding view are two projections of the same fact. Equality is **pure
> judgment** (identical after normalizing both sides; it does not bind type variables); evidence is
> the **sole entry point** for q=0 slots (four sources: literals/value environment/single-value
> pinning/Γ equality); erasure is the **runtime consequence** of q=0 (it holds for both closed and
> open/recursive terms); Σ construction points **reuse** the same evidence interface and do not
> establish a separate one. **Completion criterion = the invariants hold, not that the subphase
> names have all been run.**

> → B.d; design review → D implementation. A.C3 and B.d may proceed in parallel but require
> file-surface coordination (C3 leans toward typecheck→mono, d toward types/solver→sema); C.2 may
> proceed in parallel with B.d after 6.9.2-B/6.9.3a (it does not depend on defeq); D implementation
> waits for confirmation of the B design package and depends on A (q=0 erasure) and C.1 (dispatch),
> and may depend on the 6.9.3 typed exit. **The P7 gate = the exits of A/B/C; D does not block.**

> **A.C3 prerequisite: F4 ruling (ruled A on 2026-11-16; measured)**: the old wording “`CheckOnly`
> evidence does not enter requests” is obsolete—`ConstEvidence`/`CheckOnly` have been deleted; the
> current mechanism is that open-term `normalize` returns `Unproven` ⇒ no request is created, and
> the representation layer `GenericArg::Const(ConstExpr)` can already hold `k-1`. **The ruling
> changes to two orthogonal decisions + one termination subdecision**: D-a representation (A: open
> terms enter `deferred` and are normalized before enqueueing / B: no specialization); D-b
> evaluation point (mono only; C-1: the second field and C-2: reconstruction from IR both break the
> single representation/evaluator, so C-3 = A); **F4-T termination** (naive firing pushes the
> recursion chain into `max_depth` and hits E3005; T-a: fold the condition within the instance /
> T-b: bounded firing + fallback to the original at the boundary / T-c: a termination layer or an
> amended specification). **Measure first, then rule; before measurement, “A is immediately
> implementable” must not be treated as a conclusion.** **User (2026-11-16): D-a=A-closed, D-b=C-3,
> F4-T=T-b, bound=8; C3 implementation is a separate task, and I4 is not claimed to be complete.**

> **B.d prerequisite: decision-point protocol (not yet documented)**: RFC-027 §12.1 specifies that
> “a decision point follows the unified path first; after unified failure, it may use equality, but
> must first roll back the partial bindings produced by the unified attempt.” The implementation
> must answer: whether the entry point is a wrapper around `solver.unify` or a new `decide` layer;
> whether defeq is attempted only when both sides are ground (without unbound variables); the
> snapshot/restoration boundary and cost; and whether unify and defeq share one budget or have
> separate budgets. **Responsibility boundary**: unify continues to be responsible for
> subtyping/Any/Never; defeq only judges equivalence and does not take over subtyping; bidirectional
> subtyping must not be treated as equivalence (RFC-027 §12.1). **Provide the protocol and
> production call graph before writing code**; the 6.9.3c wiring contract already wasted two rounds
> because it assumed `can_assign` was the decision point, while `AssignmentChecker` had zero
> production instantiations.

> **E acceptance and residuals (I8, cross-cutting)**: every slice must provide ① zero
> corpus/IR-snapshot drift or an itemized classification; ② `testsuite run fast` + affected
> integration tests; ③ idempotence of the error-code generator (if an emission point/code table is
> changed); and ④ classification of behavioral changes under D59, with red before green. **Wiring
> tasks additionally require**: production call-graph evidence (which production entry point, how
> many paths, which is reachable); unit-test reachability must not be used to impersonate user
> reachability; rollback and budget must have measured numbers. **Residual handling**: #537
> (category D, proof-function formal-parameter refinement is silently discarded; do not fix before a
> ruling, and 6.9.4/6.9.5 must not depend on its fix), #539 (import-surface q=0; category-C
> boundary; if it is not closed, 6.9.4 covers only intra-module cases), #540 (deep-nesting stack
> overflow; **closed**—3.20.30 was closed on 2026-11-14: orchestration-layer 64MB large-stack
> thread + parser depth gate MAX_PARSE_DEPTH=1024 + E0019, see 09’s 3.20.30 entry), #541 (TailCall;
> **closed**—three locations moved in and out together on 2026-11-16: `call_form_is_rewritten` /
> `replace_calls_in_function` / `drop_erased_call_args` cover `Call`/`TailCall` through the
> single-point `rewritten_call_target`; the init section and function body share one site-rewriting
> implementation; red→green + three mutations), #542 (orphaned shared layer; **landed
> (2026-11-19)**: DCE pass + post-mono two entry-point wiring + C2c temporary avoidance removal;
> red→green, 402/402, function-table attribution and deviations), and #552 (multi-parameter
> predicate proof execution; adjacent to 6.9.5, separate task). **Ownership pending a ruling**: the
> four open-constraint tripwires (`Eq(N, n)`) in `rfc027_refined_transparency` do not belong to
> 6.9.4’s constant-equality bridge; whether they remain in 6.9.4’s outOfScope or move to 6.9.1/the
> E4018 proof-function surface requires a ruling.

> **Do not claim / boundary**: this item covers only record Σ (B: witness field), does not touch
> Π/`DepFn`, and does not claim that Π/Σ is complete; 6.9.4 covers only constant equalities and does
> not fulfill the `Eq(N,n)` tripwire; `f(y)(y)`’s second value position is outside this item;
> witness erasure ≠ runtime-check erasure; if #537 is not fixed, 6.9.4/6.9.5 cover only forms that
> do not depend on proof-function formal-parameter refinement; if #539 is not fixed, 6.9.4 covers
> only intra-module cases; #540 is closed (3.20.30); #542 has landed (2026-11-19); the
> inner-isolation red state in 2.1.4 was cleared on 2026-11-20 (the criterion was rewritten by slot
> identity in the 2.1.4 closure) ⇒ all prerequisites for promoting `verify` to a gate have been
> removed.

**Hard acceptance** (**criteria revised on 2026-10-27, following decision ② of 2026-10-26**):
`git diff --stat tests/yaoxiang tests/baselines src/std/` must be **empty in every round of
6.1–6.7**. **Direct-drive test files** under `tests/` (tests that directly drive the changed code,
such as `tests/formatter_integration.rs`) may be modified when mechanically required by the change,
but each must be registered with **file / line count / reason**; **tests must not be deleted and
assertions must not be weakened**. **Exception**: 6.8.2 is a **behavioral-fix** batch (new
diagnostic codes + baseline updates), does not fall under this hard acceptance criterion, and is
handled as a separate round with a separate ruling.

> **Revision relationship**: the original criterion (decision ② of 2026-10-26) was written as
> `git diff --stat tests/ src/std/`, making the entire `tests/` directory zero-diff; the revised
> criterion **changes only direct-drive test files from “zero diff” to “may be modified but must
> register file / line count / reason”**, while the zero-diff requirement for the corpus layer
> (`tests/yaoxiang`), baseline layer (`tests/baselines`), and standard library (`src/std/`) remains
> unchanged. First application = 6.1.2: only `tests/formatter_integration.rs` changed, with **3
> lines** changed (2 occurrences of `assert_format_eq` from `i64`→`Int64` + 1 comment line), with
> the reason = the expected type name in the assertion must be synchronized with the changed
> spelling; no tests were deleted and no assertions were weakened. See “P6 6.1 Name-Normalization
> Closure.”

**Risk**: the 8.4 dual-parser differential is a **non-skippable equivalence gate**. If it finds a
difference, the problem must be resolved before 8.5 switches traffic, rather than hidden after
switching by C5′. If any of the approximately 89 BP references are missed during the 8.6 migration,
it will **silently change associativity** (no error, only a different parse result).

> code refers back to `sema`, it will be blocked by `check-boundary.py`.

## Implementation Essentials: Dependencies and Parallelization

### Mandatory Serial Main Chain

`P0 → P1 → P2 → P3 → P3.5 → P4 → P5 → P6 → (P7 ∥ P8) → P9 → P10`

> **P3 stop-the-bleeding path (decision of 2026-10-05)**: P3’s prerequisites are narrowed to
> **2.3.2 + 2.4.1 + 2.4.3** (multi-file corpus layer + two red criteria). The rest of P2 (2.1 IR
> verifier, 2.2 snapshots, 2.3.1/2.3.3 differential testing and performance baseline) can proceed in
> parallel with P3. Stopping the bleeding for correctness vulnerabilities must not be blocked by
> criterion-infrastructure construction; however, **P4 must still wait for all of P2**—the unified
> Driver requires all three layers of criteria to be in place.

| Constraint         | Reason                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| P0 → P1            | The three prohibitions constrain every action in P1 (1.2.x adds `mod` declarations to `mod.rs`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| P1 → P2            | Reviving tests changes the test count and corpus baseline                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| P2 (narrowed) → P3 | Vulnerability criteria must **be written red first**—2.4.1/2.4.3 + the multi-file corpus layer 2.3.2 must exist so that red tests have somewhere to run                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| P3 → P4            | Fix bugs before refactoring; reversing the order lets bugs become “established behavior” through the phase table                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| P3.5 → P4          | RFC-029g (#399)’s deletion surface covers the rewriting targets of P4 4.2.2 / P5 / P6 / P7 / P8 (the list is in §P3.5 of this document)—reversing the order means redoing the same deletions on the new syntax, new checker layout, and new IR (D56)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| P4 → P5            | The `include!` conversion and checker splitting modify the same file                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| P5 → P6            | Consecutive changes to the same file must be separated, or regressions cannot be bisected                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| P6 → P7 / P8       | Type representations must converge first, or the new IR will grow into a third representation; **the P7 gate = the exits of phases A/B/C of 6.9** (I1–I3, I5, I7; namely 6.9.2 including C3, 6.9.3 including d, and completed 6.9.4); D (Σ) does not block; P7 may consume quantifier-derived views and the defeq interface but must not create a parallel ledger; the 7.0 pure-relocation batch is a P7 prerequisite and is not subject to this gate, but it must not consume an undecided defeq/quantifier interface |
| P7/P8 → P9         | The 9.5 snapshot baseline and the 9.3 `pub(crate)` leak count are taken in their final form only after P7/P8                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |

### Parallelization Groups

| Group                                      | Members                                                                            | Basis                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **A (the only one authorized by RFC-039)** | P7 ∥ P8                                                                            | Disjoint file sets: `ir.rs`/`ir_gen.rs`/`bytecode.rs`/`translator.rs` vs `lexer/*`/`parser/*`                                                                                                                                                         |
| B                                          | 1.2.1 ∥ 1.2.2 ∥ 1.2.3 ∥ 1.2.4                                                      | Each independently adds a `mod`; revert file by file                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| C                                          | 2.1 ∥ 2.2 ∥ 2.3.1 ∥ 2.3.2 ∥ 2.4                                                    | The three layers of criteria are mutually independent                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| D                                          | 4.4 (proof-layer wrap-up) ∥ the entire P6 track                                    | `02` explicitly states in S5 that it should proceed independently of S1–S4                                                                                                                                                                            |
| E                                          | 4.2.5 ∥ 4.2.6 ∥ 4.2.8                                                              | All are mutually independent after 4.1 is complete                                                                                                                                                                                                    |

| G                                          | S3 ∥ S4 ∥ S5                                                                       | Disjoint file sets (verified on 2026-10-05: S3 changes `docs/src/dev/design/check/` + `config.js`; S4 changes `docs/src/rfc/` + the `check_tracking.py` generator; S5 changes two `pub` sites in `src/frontend/core/typecheck/`; no pairwise overlap) |

**Cannot run in parallel (file overlap)**: P1(1.1.x) ∥ P8(8.0.x); 1.2.1 ∥ 8.3.2; 6.0 ∥ S2 (B6/E5
same-batch files); 4.3.2 ∥ 9.2 (unified under P4); **3.4 ∥ P3.5** (`checker.rs` / `environment.rs`
are the same files—the external track’s pub-deletion batch and the silent-channel fixes must be
serial).

**New internal document constraints**: 6.0→6.1→6.2→6.3→6.4→6.5→6.6 is strictly serial; 7.0 →
7a→7b→7c→7d is strictly serial (7.0 is the pure-relocation batch that precedes P7), and 7b’s `Phi`
arm must precede 7d.

## Key Decisions and Rationale

- **P0 is an independent phase rather than part of P9**—gates are “post-hoc checks,” while rules are
  “pre-hoc judgment.” P9’s scripts cannot prevent “patching when a refactor is required”; only the
  D0–D4 review checklist can do so.
- **P9 is the sole authoritative list of CI scripts**—the three coexisting lists that constituted
  original gap G3 prevented closure. After consolidation, 10 active scripts each belong to one phase
  (9.8 was cancelled by the user on 2026-11-24), and report-only status and hard-conversion timing
  are explicitly traceable.
- **P3.5 incorporates RFC-029g rather than leaving it as an “independent track to perform after the
  refactor”**—its deletion surface overlaps with the rewriting surfaces of P4/P5/P6/P7/P8 (RFC-039
  D56). Deferring it until after the refactor means redoing the same deletions on the new syntax,
  new checker layout, and new IR; this is the same lesson as incorporating `2315`/`2341` into 7e and
  RFC-status corrections into S4.
- **P5’s steps are supplied by this document rather than merged into P4**—P4 is already the largest
  single-point risk, and adding checker splitting would exceed a revertible granularity.
- **5.3.2 uses “zero caller changes” as the hard acceptance criterion**—the split must be
  independently revertible.

## Known Limitations and Risks

- **1.3.x (fixing exposed defects) has no regression criterion**—it says only that “fixed defects
  should not be rolled back,” and lacks a record requirement identifying what was fixed. **Execution
  convention**: every 1.3.x fix’s commit message must cite the fixed test name and defect
  description as evidence for later bisection.
- ~~**7b.1 is too coarse**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: split into the exclusive commits 7b.1a / 7b.1b
  per DoD 6.
- **8.2.1 is too coarse**—approximately 89 reference renames; missing one will **silently change
  associativity**.
- ~~**D17 / D20 have no corresponding level-3 tasks**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: D17 landed as 7e.1,
  and D20 landed as 4.5.1/4.5.2; D32/D34 opcode reclamation was incorporated into 7e.1, with
  deletion left in P10 S6.
- ~~**The `2315` / `2341` data-loss defects were originally designated “separate issues”**~~ **Fixed
  (2026-10-05)**: incorporated as 7e.2 / 7e.3. The exception table (throw/try) is core language
  semantics and must not be left as an implementation remnant.
- ~~**E2 (`lib.rs:568/582` `todo!()`) has no phase ownership**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**:
  incorporated into P10 S2.
- ~~**F7 (opcode gate extractor) has ambiguous ownership**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: incorporated
  into the generation-time gate task in P10 S6.

| C2              | “Grammar-driven” promise vs table-driven implementation                        | **Fallback approach**: retain Pratt + one declarative precedence table + cross-validation of two `BinOp` implementations from the same source (the LALRPOP route is withdrawn); see P8 8.3 |
| C3              | Conflict between the C6 category definition and S1 classification              | **S1 is classified under C6** (revival does not require an equivalence criterion, only regression tests); the C6 definition is expanded to “pure deletion or pure revival”                 |
| C4              | `test_release_plan_spans_consumed` whitelist                                   | **No whitelist**; the difference must be empty; if it cannot be empty, the `ReleasePlan` contract is defective → change to `PlanId` (D20/D41)                                              |
| C5              | Internal differences between the two `Aggregation` functions were not verified | **P4’s 4.2.7 explicitly lists verification as required**, to be confirmed line by line during implementation                                                                               |
| C6              | The wasm playground fix requires P4’s `ProgramKind`                            | **The wasm-path vulnerability fix is incorporated into 4.2.8**; P3 handles only the three native entry points                                                                              |
| C7              | Ownership of `method_def_ordinals`                                             | **Assigned to 04** (P7 batch c); see D21                                                                                                                                                   |
| C8              | Fixing `upvalue_count` and the `.42` version number                            | **Fix + bump `VERSION` from 4 to 5** (the format header already has `MAGIC` + `VERSION` fields, `codegen/bytecode.rs:14-16`); see D17                                                      |
